The code wins, so the lock is two blocks: src/*.ts at warn, which Testing.ts's JSON.parse fire still holds, and src/*.tsx at error. Each restates the entries these files took before from the Reflect ban's warn block: Data.TaggedError, JSON.parse and the four Reflect entries. At warn a vi fire still blocks: advice.ts lets only a fire whose message starts with 'JSON.parse' advise, and the new scenario checks that on oxlint's own warning fires. VI_PROPERTIES in oxlint-plugins/builtin-plants.ts refuses the two chained forms and one plain call of each member, and takes vi.hoisted, vi.waitFor, a comment, a string and another object's fn. VI_METHODS gains the chained lines as false, under its own code, plus the same call in parentheses as true. The Reflect scenario planted one file per glob and asserted they were all different; the Reflect warn block's src/* and the lock's src/*.ts name the same file, so it now checks each planted file once, as the Data.TaggedError scenario does. No product file changed.
